sources.title: Bengt Holmström, MIT 14.124 Microeconomic Theory IV — Lecture Slides, Part 2 (Spring 2017 course; slides dated February 2, 2016)
sources.use: Primary method reference for hidden effort and contractible outcomes, action and participation constraints, utility-space wage variables, informative performance measures and multitask attention allocation. The chapter's finite probabilities, limited-liability constraints, square-root risk example, audit and noisy-proxy technology are original and proved separately.
sources.verification: Retrieved actual official 60-page PDF and inspected extracted slide text, particularly slides 2–20 for timing, two-step effort/contract optimization, IC/IR, risk sharing and informativeness; slides 43–54 for multitasking, task interaction and performance measurement. Also inspected surrounding sufficient-statistic discussion for scope. The course is Spring 2017 while the slide front matter is dated February 2, 2016. Did not import a blanket claim that IR binds: the chapter's wage floors can produce slack IR. Did not reproduce source examples or claim inspection/proof of the continuous-time, LEN or general multitask results. Earlier retrieval of a scanned author-hosted multitask paper was not used as a verified body-text source. Verification is scoped method inspection, not whole-course certification.

sources.title: Oliver Hart, Incomplete Contracts and Control, American Economic Review 107(7), 1731–1752 (2017)
sources.use: Primary author account of incomplete contracting, residual control over assets, relationship-specific investment, hold-up, the different incentive effects of either direction of integration, and efficient ex post bargaining versus distorted ex ante investment. The chapter's binary investments, outside-option schedules, equal-split rule and compensation comparisons are original assumptions and calculations.
sources.verification: Opened Oliver Hart's official Harvard publication page and followed its PDF attachment to the actual 22-page article. Inspected extracted text of section I, especially printed pages 1732–1735: incomplete agreements and residual control; integration benefits and disempowerment costs; symmetric-information efficient renegotiation; the need for noncontractible investments; control over non-human assets. Later financial-contracting text was visible but is not relied on for chapter claims. A Nobel-site PDF attempt returned an error/403; successful verification is the distinct official author-hosted article, not that blocked URL. No claim of reviewing the complete property-rights literature, proving a general bargaining theorem or validating empirical ownership effects.
